newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia shortlists six for electronic combat kit.
newsitem.headline: Australia shortlists six for electronic combat kit.

text.p: Australia short-listed six European, U.S. and Israeli contractors on Tuesday to supply electronic warfare systems for combat aircraft, transports and helicopters.

"The six potential suppliers are British Aerospace Australia, Lockheed Martin, Northrop Grumman, Raytheon E-Systems, Rockwell-ASTA Defence (a Boeing Company unit) and a combined team of Elta and Elisra from Israel," Defence Minister Ian McLachlan said in a statement.
Elisra is a unit of Tadiran Ltd. Elta is state-owned.
"The entire project, known as Echidna ... involves threat-warning and countermeasures systems to protect the aircraft from guided weapons systems," McLachlan said.
The equipment would be fitted to F-111 strike bombers, UH-60 Black Hawk utility helicopters, CH-47 Chinook transport helicopters and C-130J Hercules transports.
McLachlan said Australia would request tenders later this year and expected to sign a contract in mid-1999.
